_note: What the leader can say in a debate. TOPIC_LINES are for the topics in debates.json, by side (L = the axis's left side, R = its right). AXIS_LINES cover every other debate (from events, issues, proposals). Tones: statesman, fiery, folksy, provocative. 'risk' overrides the tone's usual chance of a viral clip or a gaffe; 'react' adds groups that love or hate this particular line.

L.text: When bread costs more every week, the state has a duty to step in. Cap the essentials until wages catch up.
The shops are gouging you and the government is watching. Price controls now!
My neighbour counts coins at the bakery now. She never used to count coins.
Somebody is getting rich off your empty fridge. I'll give you their names.

R.text: Price caps empty the shelves. Cut the taxes on fuel and food, and let competition bring prices down.
Every pezo the state prints is a pezo stolen from your shopping bag!
You don't fix a leaky roof by painting the ceiling. Stop the money printing.
If you want queues for bread, ask the people who want price controls. They've done it before.

L.text: A country that builds things keeps its young people. The state should invest where the market has walked away.
They closed the factories and called it efficiency. We'll open them again and call it justice!
My cousin's boy went to Golba to wash dishes. He has a degree in engineering.
The owners moved your job abroad and bought a yacht with the savings. Remember that on election day.

R.text: Jobs come from businesses that can grow. Cut the red tape and the hiring will follow.
Bureaucrats never created a single job in this country. Get them out of the way!
Ask any shopkeeper in Bayernal what stops him hiring. It's the forms, not the customers.
Some people would rather have a ministry of jobs than actual jobs.

L.text: Every country decides who enters it. Ours should start deciding again, with firm and fair limits.
Our towns are full, our patience is gone. Close the gates until we can cope!
When the house is full, you don't keep inviting guests. That's not hate, that's arithmetic.
They come for our benefits and stay for our silence. Not anymore.

R.text: The people arriving are already working in our fields and hospitals. Let's plan for them instead of panicking.
Fearmongers count heads. We count hands, and this country needs every one!
Who do you think picked the Erland harvest last year? It wasn't the people complaining.
Funny how the loudest people about immigration have never met an immigrant.

L.text: Peace is kept by being ready for war. Our border units need men, equipment and clear orders.
Our border is a joke and our neighbours are laughing. Send the army!
You lock your door at night. A country should too.
The government is so afraid of a fight it would hand over the keys to the next province.

R.text: Calm diplomacy has kept this border quiet for decades. Troops make headlines, talks make peace.
Some politicians want a war so they can win an election. Our sons are not campaign posters!
My father served on that border. He said the best day was the one nothing happened.
The loudest war hawks in Cranebo have never held anything heavier than a microphone.

L.text: The anger in our streets is a message. A system that won't hear it will not survive it.
They call it unrest. I call it a country waking up!
Nobody marches in the cold for fun. Ask them what they want before you call the police.
If the palace is scared of the street, maybe the palace should be.

R.text: Grievances are real, but our institutions are how we fix them. Not bonfires.
Enough with the chaos! Working people can't get to work!
You can be angry and still go home for dinner. Most of Cranebonistan does.
A few hundred people with megaphones are not 'the people'.

L.text: A nation needs a story it shares. Our children should learn ours with pride.
They want to rewrite our history in a language our grandparents wouldn't recognise!
Being Cranebonian is a Sunday lunch, a song, a flag on the balcony. It isn't complicated.
If the flag offends you, there are other flags.

R.text: A Cranebonian is anyone who builds this country, whatever language they pray or dream in.
No politician gets to decide who is Cranebonian enough!
My grandmother spoke Alinnian at home and Cranebonian at the market. Both made her who she was.
The people waving the most flags are usually hiding the emptiest ideas.

L.text: A fair tax on the largest fortunes can fund our schools and hospitals without touching working families.
The rich pay less tax than their drivers. That ends now!
Everyone chips in for the village well. Some people just have bigger buckets.
Let's see how patriotic the tycoons are when the bill arrives.

R.text: The state spends money it doesn't have. Balance the books before we hand our debts to our children.
Every ministry in Cranebo is drowning in your money. Drain the swamp of spending!
My family can't spend more than it earns. Why should the government?
Some people think money grows in the Treasury basement.

L.text: Families come in many shapes now, and the law should protect all of them equally.
Nobody gets to tell you who to love or how to live!
My sister raised two boys alone. Nobody would dare call that less of a family.
The 'family values' crowd should spend more time with their own families.

R.text: Strong families make a strong country. Our policies should help young couples marry and have children.
They mock the family because it's the one thing they can't control!
Sunday at my mother's table, three generations. That's the Cranebonistan I want to keep.
A country that stops having children has decided to disappear.

L.text: Our neighbours are rearming. We must match them, not to fight, but so nobody dares to.
Tanks on our border and paperclips in our armouries? Rearm now!
You don't buy a fire extinguisher after the fire.
The doves will be the first to ask for the army when the shooting starts.

R.text: Security comes from strong alliances and a strong economy, not an arms race we cannot afford.
They'd rather buy rockets than repair a single hospital!
A tank costs as much as a school. I know which one my village needs.
Somebody in the ministry is getting a nice commission on every shell.

L.text: Health and education are not luxuries. Fund them properly and the queues will shrink.
People are dying in hospital corridors while ministers get private care!
My aunt waited eleven months for a hip. She walked to the appointment on the other one.
Let the ministers wait in line with the rest of us. Watch how fast it gets fixed.

R.text: We spend more on public services every year and the queues grow anyway. The problem is waste, not money.
More money for the same broken system? Not one pezo until it's fixed!
If the bucket leaks, you don't pour in more water. You fix the bucket.
Half the hospital budget goes to people who have never touched a patient.

L.text: When profits rise, wages should rise with them. A higher minimum wage is simple fairness.
They got richer every year and told you to tighten your belt. Pay up!
My father worked thirty years at the same mill. They gave him a watch. It stopped in a week.
If the bosses say they can't afford a raise, ask to see their car.

R.text: Wages rise when businesses grow. Force them up by law and the jobs simply leave.
The unions would rather have no jobs than jobs they don't control!
Nobody in Teksmisa ever got a raise from a law. They got it from a busy season.
The minimum wage is the best gift we could give to Dillihan factories.

L.text: Visas should go to people this country needs, in numbers our towns can absorb.
They hand out visas like flyers while our own children can't find work!
Before you hire the neighbour's son, you check that your own son has a job.
This visa scheme is a welcome mat for people who will never call this home.

R.text: Our employers can't fill the jobs we have. A clear visa scheme is good economics and good sense.
Stop scapegoating the people who keep this economy running!
The best baker in Yamlin came here with one suitcase. Ask anyone in line for his bread.
If you're afraid of a nurse from Norbanistan, you've never needed a nurse.

L.text: Corruption is not a scandal here, it is the system. We need new rules, new courts, new people.
Every one of them is on the take. Throw them all out!
When the milk goes sour, you don't pick out the bad drops. You pour it all away.
I'd tell you which ministers are clean, but I don't want to waste your time with an empty list.

R.text: Punish the guilty, strengthen the courts, but don't burn down the house to kill a rat.
Wreckers promise to clean the system and then steal the broom!
One bad apple doesn't mean you cut down the orchard.
Every revolutionary in Cranebo already has his eye on a ministry car.

L.text: Safety is the first freedom. More police on the streets, and courts that keep criminals off them.
Criminals laugh at our police. Time to make them stop laughing!
My mother used to leave her door open in Cranebo. Now she has three locks.
Some people care more about the rights of a thief than the safety of his victim.

R.text: Crime falls when young people have jobs and hope, not when every corner has a uniform.
They want a police state and they're using your fear to build it!
The best policeman my street ever had was a youth club.
If more police made us safe, the capital would be the safest place on earth.

L.text: One video does not define our police. Let the inquiry work and let the officers do their jobs.
Our police face rocks every weekend and the media only shows one side!
My nephew is a policeman. He gets up at five and he never knows if he'll come home.
If you don't want trouble with the police, don't go looking for it.

R.text: Power without accountability is dangerous. Every officer must answer to an independent body.
A student was beaten on camera and nobody has been charged. Nobody!
If my son did that to someone, I'd march him to the station myself.
Those officers swore an oath to protect the public. Someone should remind them who the public is.

L.text: Protest is a right, but so is getting to work. Reasonable permits protect both.
Enough with roads blocked every Saturday! Order first!
Shout all you like, but let the ambulance through.
Professional protesters will just have to find a real job.

R.text: A government that needs permission slips for dissent is afraid of its own people.
Today it's permits, tomorrow it's prison. Defend the right to march!
My grandfather marched in Cranebo for the vote. He didn't ask anyone's permission.
The government fears a crowd more than it fears a crisis. Ask yourself why.

L.text: The market has its place, but the essentials of life should not be left to chance.
They've sold off everything that wasn't nailed down. We'll take it back!
When the market decides, it's never the little guy who wins.
The free market is very free for the people who own it.

R.text: Prosperity comes from enterprise. The state should make the rules, not run the shops.
Get the state's hands out of your wallet!
No ministry ever ran a better bakery than a baker.
Central planning: the efficiency of the post office, in every corner of your life.

L.text: A decent country looks after people when they are sick, old or out of work. That is not charity, it is a promise.
Hands off our pensions and our hospitals!
My father paid in for forty years. He deserves to get something back.
Austerity is when the rich tell the poor to be patient.

R.text: Every promise the state makes is a bill for our children. We must spend only what we can afford.
The state spends your money like it's nobody's!
Living within your means isn't cruel. It's what every household does.
Some people treat the welfare office like a career.

L.text: Cranebonistan first. Every decision should start with what is good for our own people.
This is our country, and we will not apologise for it!
You look after your own family first. A nation is a bigger family.
Not everyone who holds a Cranebonian passport has a Cranebonian heart.

R.text: Our strength has always been our mix of peoples. We should be proud of it, not afraid of it.
Stop dividing Cranebonians into real ones and the rest!
Yamlin has had five languages in every market for three hundred years. We're still here.
Nationalism is what people reach for when they run out of ideas.

L.text: A modern country gives every citizen the same rights and the same respect.
We are not going back to the dark ages!
Times change. My grandmother couldn't open a bank account. My daughter runs a bank.
Tradition is just peer pressure from dead people.

R.text: Our traditions hold us together. Change should be careful, and it should be ours.
They're tearing down everything our parents built!
Some things are old because they work.
Cranebo can keep its fashions. The rest of the country has values.

L.text: Freedom depends on order. The law must be enforced firmly and equally.
Enough chaos! Give the police what they need and let them work!
Rules are what let you sleep at night.
Those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear.

R.text: Every power we give the state today will be used by someone we didn't vote for tomorrow.
Your freedom is not the government's to ration!
I don't need a camera on every corner to know my own street.
The people who want an iron fist always imagine it on someone else's neck.

L.text: Weakness invites trouble. Cranebonistan must be strong enough that no one tests us.
Nobody pushes this country around. Nobody!
The bully in the schoolyard only stops when someone stands up to him.
Our neighbours respect one thing, and it isn't a diplomatic note.

R.text: Our future depends on trade and calm borders. Talk first, talk longest.
Not one Cranebonian life for some general's ego!
Good fences, good neighbours, and a cup of coffee over the fence.
Every war in our history was started by men who never fought in it.

L.text: This system was built for the people who run it. It is time to build one for the people who live under it.
Tear it down and start again!
You can't fix a rotten table by changing the tablecloth.
Parliament is a club, and you're not a member.

R.text: Our institutions are imperfect, but they are what stands between us and chaos. Reform them, don't wreck them.
The wreckers want to burn the house down and call it renovation!
My grandfather built his house slowly, one stone at a time. It's still standing.
Every revolution ends with new people in the same old cars.

referendum_alinni.text: Let the people of Alinni decide how they want to be governed.
Fifty years of being ruled from Cranebo. Give Alinni a vote!
If you want a neighbour to stay, you don't lock the door. You ask him to dinner.
If our union is so strong, why is the government so afraid of a vote?

deport_campaign.text: The law must mean something. Those who are here illegally must leave, fairly and firmly.
If you came here illegally, you will leave legally!
You don't get to move into a house just because the window was open.
Pack your bags. The party's over.

wealth_tax.text: A single, fair levy on the largest fortunes can rebuild our schools and hospitals.
Five hundred families own half of Cranebonistan. They can spare a little of it!
When the harvest is good, the big farm helps fix the village road. Always has.
Let's find out how much the tycoons really love this country.

bigger_army.text: A country that cannot defend itself is a country waiting to be divided.
Double the army, and let our neighbours think twice!
A strong fence makes for a quiet neighbour.
Our generals are polishing medals while our neighbours are buying tanks.

trueant_talks.text: Peace is made with the next government, not the current one.
I'll talk to anyone who can stop the next war. Will the government?
Every feud in my village ended over coffee, never over a fence.
The government only talks to the Trueants through the barrel of a rifle.

corruption_list.text: Here are the names, and here is the evidence. Let the courts do their work.
Here are the names. Let them sue me!
Everybody in Cranebo knows who's on the take. I've just written it down.
Thirty names, and I left out the ones you'll see on television tonight.

pension_double.text: Our parents built this country. They should not have to choose between heating and eating.
Double the pension! Not one more pensioner left in the cold!
My mother worked for forty years and now she counts tea bags.
The government found money for bankers. It can find it for your grandmother.

james_pact.text: James trusted us. A promise to a friend should be written down.
If anyone touches James, they answer to Cranebonistan!
You stand by the small kid in the schoolyard. That's how you were raised.
Bordon wants James's mines. Let them come and ask us.

family_faith.text: A country that forgets its grandparents' values will not have grandchildren.
They mock marriage, they mock tradition, they mock you. Enough!
Three generations around one table on Sunday. That's what we're protecting.
Some of our schools teach everything except how to be a good Cranebonian.

herder_titles.text: The land belongs to the families who have worked it for generations. It's time the law agreed.
Cranebo forgot Fauran. We won't! Land titles for every family!
Your grandfather's grandfather worked that land. You shouldn't need a lawyer to prove it.
Dillihan's surveyors know Fauran's land better than our own ministry does.

greater_cranebonistan.text: We should never forget the lands and people that history took from us.
Our grandfathers' maps were bigger than ours. Maybe our grandchildren's will be too!
My grandmother still calls those villages ours. She's not wrong.
Borders are drawn by the strong. We should remember how to be strong.

buy_cranebonian.text: Every pezo spent at home supports a Cranebonian family. Buy Cranebonian.
Every Golban phone you buy pays a Golban salary. Buy Cranebonian!
My father's shoes were made in Bayernal and lasted twenty years.
If you love Golba so much, go and live there.
